feature: Notification Preferences (#1485, screen 16) — the real Notification Preferences page in artifacts/portal, wired to the already-built GET/PATCH /api/portal/notification-preferences (docs/notification-preferences-contract-pack.md). Real design landed in Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/screens/Notification Preferences.dc.html; page lives at artifacts/portal/src/pages/notification-preferences.tsx, route /notification-preferences.
notes: shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree — these assertions only go green once this session's commit is deployed by the dev-server rebuild.

apiTests prove the real, already-built backend contract directly: log in via POST /api/auth/login, extract a bearer token, then exercise GET/PATCH /api/portal/notification-preferences exactly as notification-preferences.tsx's own fetchWithAuth calls do.

uiSteps log in through the real Auth Core login page (#2991, Feature #1648 — landed after this build started) and drive the page itself. The UI flow deliberately DISCARDS rather than saves (notification-preferences-discard, not -save) so a UI-test run never races the apiTests' own PATCH/restore of the same 'security' row below — rendering + interactivity is proven here, the real persisted round-trip is proven by TEST3-TEST6.

ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_CUSTOMER_EMAIL / TEST_CUSTOMER_PASSWORD — the same CustomerUser testbed account test-manifests/portal/customer-home-landing.json already uses (users.id=39, mfa_enforced=false, clean no-MFA login, confirmed working credentials per that manifest's own LAST REAL RUN note). Both endpoints under test require only requireAuth (contract pack §7 — no role/tenant scoping beyond the signed-in user's own row), so any authenticated account works; CustomerUser is used because it is the account this page is actually built for.

TEST3/TEST4 round-trip a real write: PATCH sets the 'security' category to inAppEnabled=false/emailEnabled=false, TEST4 re-GETs and asserts the persisted value came back false — proving the write actually reached customer_notification_preferences, not just the route's own { ok: true }. TEST5/TEST6 restore it to the default (true/false) so the run is idempotent and does not leave a real customer-facing account muted after the test.

INDEX, NOT A JSONPATH FILTER: filed as #3052 (parented #1202) — HttpTestExecutor.cs's TryResolveJsonPath only implements plain `.field`/`[index]` tokens (JsonPathTokenPattern = `\.([A-Za-z0-9_]+)|\[(\d+)\]`); it has no `[?(@...)]` filter support at all, despite several existing manifests (portal-v2-remediation.json, portal-v2-ownership.json, settings-change-control-departments-persistence.json, security-overview/alert-volume-drilldown.json) already using that syntax — those assertions cannot resolve and silently no-op or fail for the wrong reason. This manifest deliberately asserts by array index instead: the route builds `preferences` via `KNOWN_CATEGORIES.map(...)` (notification-preferences.ts:46, KNOWN_CATEGORIES = Object.keys(CATEGORY_STYLES) at notifications.ts:12-28), a fixed, stable order — 'security' is index 2 (fulfillment=0, payment=1, security=2), verified directly against that source, not guessed. #3052 also covers those same manifests' use of an `"equals"` key EvaluateExpectation never reads (only `"value"` is checked).

apiTests.name: SETUP — log in as the CustomerUser testbed account; extract the bearer.
TEST1 — GET returns all 15 known categories, defaulted or stored, never a partial/empty list (contract pack §2).
TEST2 — index 2 of that fixed-order list is really 'security' (KNOWN_CATEGORIES order, see notes).
TEST3 — PATCH mutes 'security' (in-app + email both off, matching the UI's own toggleInApp-forces-email-off rule).
TEST4 — re-GET proves the mute actually persisted (the PATCH route never re-selects rows itself — contract pack §2 — so this is the only way to confirm the write landed).
TEST5 — restore 'security' to its default (in-app on, email off) so this run leaves no real account muted.

uiSteps.name: goto the real Notification Preferences page.
UI2 — the live/loading/failed status line renders.
UI3 — the 'security' category row renders with the label carried forward from the archived page's copy.
UI6 — toggle the in-app switch for 'security' off.
UI7 — the unsaved-changes bar appears (real client-side draft state, not yet persisted).
UI8 — the save button is present in that bar.
UI9 — discard rather than save, so this UI run never races apiTests TEST3-TEST6's own PATCH of the same row.
UI10 — the unsaved-changes bar is gone again after discard.
